issues.detail: Examples describe scenarios and expected outputs at a high level but lack concrete step-by-step walkthroughs or actual code demonstrations with realistic data transformations.

scenarios.name: mysql-postgresql-encoding-conversion
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly satisfies all rubric requirements: DATETIME→TIMESTAMPTZ with explicit timezone decision, ENUM→PostgreSQL ENUM with DDL, and UTF-8 re-encoding planning with specific commands. Response A fails on two critical requirements by recommending timestamp-without-timezone instead of TIMESTAMPTZ and advocating a lookup table instead of the rubric-specified ENUM/VARCHAR-with-CHECK options, though it excels on encoding conversion depth with hex dumps and pgloader details.

scenarios.name: large-table-batch-migration-checkpoint
scenarios.rationale: Response B covers the rubric completely: it specifies the exact 5000-row batch size, implements proper lastId-based checkpoint/resume with WHERE pk > lastId pattern, shows disabling triggers and rebuilding with REINDEX, and clearly demonstrates resumption detection. Response A uses a 10k default (not the recommended 5000), implements offset-based pagination rather than the efficient lastId pattern, and critically omits any guidance on disabling/rebuilding indexes—a mandatory rubric requirement.

scenarios.name: circular-dependency-referential-validation
scenarios.rationale: A directly addresses topological sort and FK dropping as required, with clear dependency ordering and orphan checks, but lacks aggregate/row-count validation; B sidesteps topological sort via constraint disabling, has superior orphan detection queries, but explicitly avoids the core requirement and also omits aggregate checks.
